p and bring it back, with no console window.
# dsh-restart-foot
A restart button for the DeepSeek Harness **desktop app**, placed at the **sidebar foot — directly a
bove the avatar / Settings entry**.
> **English** — One row in the sidebar's foot area that stops the whole application (main process, r
enderers, and the DSH host itself) and starts it again, so freshly installed plugins and settings ta
ke effect without quitting by hand. Desktop shell only.
> **中文** — 在 DSH 桌面端侧栏底部、头像/设置入口的**正上方**加一枚「重启 DeepSeek Harness」按钮：点击两次确认后，结束整个应用（主进程、渲染进程、宿主自身）并重新拉
端侧栏底部、头像/设置入口的**正上方**加一枚「重启 DeepSeek Harness」按钮：点击两次确认后，结束整个应用（主进程、渲染进程、宿主自身）并重新拉起。装完插件、改完配置不用手动退出了。
## Where the button sits / 位置

The row registers in the `sidebar.footer.action` slot. The sidebar's foot area is a vertical stack
(

`.footArea` → `.footerActions` → `.settingsArea`), so this list renders **directly above** the
setti

terActions` → `.settingsArea`), so this list renders **directly above** the
settings / account seat:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

> Note: the pop-up menu behind the avatar (Settings / Feedback / Sign out) is rendered by the
> ship

ped package `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-settings-account` (`AccountMenu`) with hard-coded
> rows and

**no insert slot**. This plugin therefore places the button in the foot row above that
> menu rathe
r than inside it — the only additive option that does not shadow shipped UI.
## Behaviour / 行为
- **First click** arms the button (it turns into the error colour and reads “Click again to confirm”

; it falls back to idle after 5 s).
- **Second click** sends `POST /dsh-restart-foot/restart`. The h

ost writes a `cmd` batch and starts it through `wscript.exe`.
- **No console window**: `wscript.exe`
is a GUI-subsystem program, so Windows never gives it a console; it runs the batch with a hidden wi
ndow style. The helper is started **detached** anyway, because the desktop application owns its chil
dren through a job object — an ordinary child is killed together with the application and would neve

r finish the restart. Detaching is what makes it survive; `wscript` is what makes it invisible.
- Th
e batch waits 1 s so the HTTP reply reaches the page, stops every process of the application image,
**polls until the image is really gone** (up to 20 s), force-stops leftovers by pid, and only then s
tarts the executable again. Waiting matters: starting a second copy while the first is still shuttin

g down is what makes the shell report a broken installation or an already-running instance.
- **`ELE
CTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` is cleared before the relaunch.** The host runs with that flag — the desktop shel
l starts the DSH host from the application binary in Node mode — so a helper that inherits it and st
arts the binary would get a plain Node process with no script, which exits at once. That failure loo

ks exactly like “it closed and never came back”, and it is the reason this line exists.
- After star
ting, the batch **verifies that the application appears** (up to 20 s) and logs `application is back

` or a warning, so the log alone tells you which step failed.
- Two helpers are written — the `wscri
pt` launcher and the bare batch as a fallback — and each is tried detached first, then hidden. Launc
h failures are never swallowed: the page shows the reason (hover the button) and `/ping` keeps it in

`lastLaunchError`.
- Log: `%TEMP%\dsh-restart-foot.log` (one line per step: request, stop, wait rou

nds, force-stop, start, back / did-not-appear).
[该节后续省略]
## Requirements / 环境要求
- DeepSeek Harness **desktop app** on Windows. The client half registers only when the page origin i

s
`dsh-app:`; in a plain browser (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>`) there is no application to relaunch, so

the
row is not registered at all.
- The host half refuses with `501` unless `process.execPath` real

ly is an application executable
(`node.exe` from a terminal `dsh web` is rejected).
- Node 20+. No b
uild step, no runtime npm dependencies.

## Routes / 路由
| Method | Path | Purpose |
| `GET` | `/dsh-restart-foot/ping` | Liveness probe: platform, whether a desktop target was found, t

he executable path, the resolved PowerShell path, and `lastLaunchError`. |
| `POST` | `/dsh-restart-
foot/restart` | Schedules the restart. Requires the `x-dsh-restart-foot: 1` header, which keeps stra
y GETs, prefetchers and other tabs from stopping the app; a cross-origin caller cannot set it withou

t a CORS preflight this server never grants. |
| `POST` | `/dsh-restart-foot/restart?probe=1` | Repo

rts the target without touching any process. |
| `POST` | `/dsh-restart-foot/selfcheck` | Diagnostic
: starts `cmd` / PowerShell probes that only write marker files and run a `taskkill` against a nonex
istent image, then reports exit codes and captured stderr. Touches no real process. Same header requ
image, then reports exit codes and captured stderr. Touches no real process. Same header required. |
If a click seems to do nothing, this is the order to look in: the button's tooltip (the failure text

),
`/dsh-restart-foot/ping` (`lastLaunchError`), `/dsh-restart-foot/selfcheck` (which launch kinds t

his host
can actually start), then `%TEMP%\dsh-restart-foot.log` (what the helper itself did).
The routes are served by the DSH web server and are reachable from any client that can reach the por

are served by the DSH web server and are reachable from any client that can reach the port;
